title: Ajvar
description: Roasted red pepper relish cooked down until a spoon dragged through it leaves a track. An autumn job done in bulk — this makes roughly three jars, sixteen servings of a spoonful each on bread.
notes: Long red horn peppers have thick walls and low water, which is why they are worth hunting down. Bell peppers work but give a thinner, sweeter result and take longer to cook down.

ingredients.name: red peppers
ingredients.note: long horn peppers if you can find them

steps.text: Roast the red peppers and the aubergines whole in a hot oven, turning them, until the skins are blistered and black in patches all over.
Tip the hot vegetables into a bowl, cover it, and leave them to steam themselves loose.
steps.tip: Steaming is what lets the skin slide off in sheets. Peel them straight from the oven and you spend an hour picking at scraps.

steps.text: Peel, stem, and seed everything, then leave the flesh piled in a colander overnight to drain.
steps.tip: This is the step people skip and then wonder why their ajvar is soup. Drained flesh fries; wet flesh boils.

steps.text: Chop the drained flesh coarsely by hand, or pulse it in short bursts — it should keep some body rather than become a purée.
Cook it in the sunflower oil over low heat, stirring often, until it darkens to brick red and a spoon dragged across the base leaves a channel that stays open.
steps.tip: The whole cook is just driving off water. Stop when the channel holds for a count of three — any further and it turns to paste on cooling.

steps.text: Stir in the garlic, chilli, salt, sugar, and red wine vinegar and cook a few minutes more to take the raw edge off.
Pot it into warm sterilised jars while hot and float a thin film of oil over the surface of each.
